name: Pound cake
origin: Named for its founding ratio, documented in English recipe collections from the early 18th century onward: a pound each of flour, sugar, butter and eggs, easy to remember before written recipes with precise weights were common.

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat softened butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, mechanically incorporating the air the batter has no other way to gain

process.name: add eggs
process.description: beat in eggs one at a time, fully emulsifying each before the next

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in the flour and salt in stages, mixing only enough to combine

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in a buttered and floured loaf pan

notes: The literal, definitional 1:1:1:1 ratio by weight (Wayne Gisslen, Professional Baking, ch. 'Cakes and Icings', and effectively every English-language baking reference since the recipe's naming). structureIndex evaluates to exactly 0 for this ratio — see formulation.spec.ts's own POUND_CAKE fixture for the same figure — matching pound cake's real reputation as a dense, moist cake sitting right at the edge of setting, no chemical leavening required or traditionally used.
